info.title: reseek
info.description: A Soulseek client daemon: its configuration, transfers, searches, chat and shares.

get.summary:
The activity log's entries, oldest first: the last few hundred things other users did with
us since the daemon started. The `activity` topic of the event stream sends the same entries,
then each new one.
The analysis reports, newest first, without their windows.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: only reports that finished after this time

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many matching reports to skip, 0 when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many reports to return at most, 100 when left out

post.summary:
Queues many files for analysis in their order, each left alone when its report is current.
What the queue has no room for is kept and joins it as it drains.

get.summary: The analyses queued and running, and how many files of batches wait for room in the queue.

delete.summary:
Takes every waiting analysis off the queue, with the files of batches waiting for room in
it. The analyses running go on; each is stopped on its own.
Takes a queued analysis off the queue, or stops a running one.

post.summary:
Takes a file from the caller's machine into the analysis cache, to analyze and play under the
`temporary` root. It leaves no report, mark or judgment and goes when the cache needs the room
or the daemon restarts. A principal uploads one file at a time, and a body that stops coming
for a minute is given up.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the file's name on the uploader's machine, which keeps its extension

get.summary:
The application state: the version, the server connection, our user, shares, rooms and
what waits for a restart or a reconnect.

put.summary:
Stops the daemon in order and exits so it starts again: with code 75 for a supervisor such
as systemd to restart it, or by starting itself again when it runs unsupervised. Needs
someone at the UI, not an API key.

delete.summary: Stops the daemon in order and exits. Needs someone at the UI, not an API key.

get.summary: The database files with their sizes on disk; empty while the databases are in memory.

post.summary:
Rebuilds a database file without its free pages, then empties its write-ahead log into
it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the database's name, as the listing gives it

put.summary:
Changes the password of our Soulseek account. Takes being logged in; refused when the
environment or the command line sets the password, since the next login would use that one.

get.summary: Our privileges, asked of the server now; the state document takes them too.

put.summary:
Sets us online or away, as other users see us; away lasts until it is set back. The server
is told at once while logged in, else at the next login.

get.summary: The running version, such as `"0.1.0"`.

The running version and the newest release the last check found. `forceCheck` checks now,
which takes the ReadWrite role.

parameters.name: forceCheck
parameters.description:
read the release feed now instead of returning what the last check found; needs
ReadWrite or above

post.summary:
Where the provider ends sessions it started, with a signed logout token naming its session
or its user. Answered 404 for a provider that takes no back-channel logout whatever the
body, else always 200, a body that is not a logout form included.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the provider's name in the configuration

get.summary:
Where the provider sends the browser back to: checks the login, signs the user in with a
session cookie and returns them to the page they came from.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the provider's name in the configuration

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: the authorization code to exchange, null when the provider sent an error

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: the value sent with the login, matched against the login cookie

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: the provider's error code when it refused the login

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: the provider's explanation of `error`, shown on the login page as text

302.description: signed in, or to the login page with the provider's error

403.description: the account is not let in

get.summary: Sends the browser to the provider's login, remembering the login in a sealed cookie.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the provider's name in the configuration

parameters.name: redirect
parameters.description:
the path on this site to return to after the login, `/` when left out; anything that is
not a path on this site is refused

post.summary: Reads a provider's discovery document now and reports what it names.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the provider's name in the configuration

get.summary:
The pinned chats in the user's order, those of a room left or a conversation closed included,
with the list's revision.

put.summary:
Replaces the pinned chats with the list given, in its order, and answers the list with the
revision the change made. The server's notices cannot be pinned, a chat is named once, and
at most 100 chats are pinned.

get.summary:
The conversations, without their messages, by username; the server's notices only with
`includeServer`.

parameters.name: unAcknowledgedOnly
parameters.description: list only conversations with unacknowledged messages

parameters.name: includeServer
parameters.description: also list the conversation holding the server's notices

get.summary:
One conversation, active or not, with its latest messages unless `includeMessages` is
false.

put.summary:
Acknowledges every unacknowledged message from a user, so the server stops sending them
again.

post.summary:
Sends a private message, the body a JSON string. The server keeps it for a user who is
offline. Line breaks become spaces, as the server drops a message holding one.

delete.summary:
Acknowledges a conversation and hides it until the next message; `purge` also deletes its
messages.

put.summary: Keeps the unsent text of a conversation, up to 4 KiB.

get.summary: The whole conversation as a file to save, JSON or text.
A page of one conversation's messages, oldest first; `before` pages back from a message.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: only messages stored before the one with this `localId`, the newest when left out

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
only messages stored after the one with this `localId`, the page then holding the oldest
of them

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many messages to return, at most 1000

put.summary: When a conversation notifies: every message, mentions only, or never.
Acknowledges one message from a user by the server's id for it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the server's id of the message

get.summary:
A page of the event log, newest first, or oldest first after `since`; `X-Total-Count` is
how many match the type and username filters.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many matching events to skip, 0 when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many events to return at most, at least 1; 100 when left out

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: only events of these types: comma-separated names in any case; every type when left out

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: only events whose data has this `username`

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: only events after this time, oldest first

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: only events before this time, newest first

post.summary:
Raises a sample event of a type, its data made up with every text starting with the body,
a JSON string that may be empty. It is logged and runs every script that takes it, exactly
as a real one does.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: the event type, in any case

get.summary: A root directory with what is in it, or everything under it with `recursive`.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: list every entry under the directory, not only its direct entries

get.summary: A directory under a root with what is in it, or everything under it with `recursive`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the directory's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: list every entry under the directory, not only its direct entries

delete.summary: Deletes a directory under a root and everything in it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the directory's path under the root, base64

get.summary: A directory under a root as a zip archive, streamed. One archive per principal at a time.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the directory's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the archive's name without `.zip`, null for the directory's name

delete.summary: Deletes a file under a root.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

get.summary: A file's analysis report; without `windows` the per-window measures are left out.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: windows
parameters.description: include the per-window measures, true when left out

post.summary: Queues a file for analysis, again with `force` when it has a report.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: analyze again even when a report for the file as it is now exists

put.summary: Records the user's own verdict on a file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

delete.summary: Takes the user's verdict on a file away.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

get.summary: The spectrum of every analyzed window of a file, in the order of its report's windows.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

200.description: a four-byte little-endian length, a WindowSpectra header as JSON, then the spectra

304.description: the caller has these bytes already, by their ETag

get.summary:
A file's spectrogram: the overview of its whole length, or with `tile` that tile at full
detail. A link token does not load it; the session does.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: tile
parameters.description: the tile at full detail, from 0; the overview of the whole file when left out

200.description: a four-byte little-endian length, a SpectrogramTile header as JSON, then its columns

304.description: the caller has these bytes already, by their ETag

get.summary:
A file's waveform: the overview of its whole length, or with `tile` that tile at full
detail.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: tile
parameters.description: the tile at full detail, from 0; the overview of the whole file when left out

200.description: a four-byte little-endian length, a WaveformTile header as JSON, then its buckets

304.description: the caller has these bytes already, by their ETag

get.summary: The spectrum of one window of a file's analysis, over linear frequency bins.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: the window's position in the report's windows

get.summary:
A file's bytes for the browser to show or save, a single range honored. A link without a
session loads it with the token `t`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: whether the browser shows the file or saves it

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name the browser saves the file under, null for the file's own name

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a file token for this file, for a link that carries no session

head.summary: The headers a file's bytes would be served with, without the bytes.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: whether the browser shows the file or saves it

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name the browser saves the file under, null for the file's own name

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a file token for this file, for a link that carries no session

200.description: the headers of the whole file

206.description: the headers of the range asked for

get.summary:
A file as a WAV made as it is read, for AIFF and ALAC, which browsers cannot play: never
stored, a single range honored. Anything else, and AIFF that is compressed, is refused.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: whether the browser shows the file or saves it

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name the browser saves the file under, null for the file's own name

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a file token for this file, for a link that carries no session

head.summary: The headers a file's WAV would be served with, without the bytes.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the file's path under the root, base64

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: whether the browser shows the file or saves it

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name the browser saves the file under, null for the file's own name

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a file token for this file, for a link that carries no session

200.description: the headers of the whole WAV

206.description: the headers of the range asked for

get.summary: What we like and hate.

put.summary:
Replaces what we like and hate and answers with the lists kept, trimmed, lowercased and
without repeats. The server is told what changed, now when logged in and at the next login
otherwise.

get.summary: Interests popular across the whole network.
Interests the server recommends to us from what we like and hate.
Users whose interests are like ours, most alike first.
Interests recommended to those who like one interest.
Users who like one interest.

The event stream: `hello`, a snapshot of each topic that has one, then every frame of the
topics as it happens. A client reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` gets what it missed when it
is still kept, else fresh snapshots and `lagged`.

parameters.name: topics
access_token
parameters.description:
an API token or a configuration API key, for clients that cannot set an
`Authorization` header; never a session cookie's value

get.summary: The log files.
One log file's text, ranges honored. The name is a bare file name ending in `.log`.
The latest log records kept in memory, oldest first.

Searches what was said in conversations and rooms. `q` is a full-text query: words,
`"phrases"`, `OR`, `NOT` and `prefix*`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: a full-text query, at most 200 characters

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: only messages by or with this user

get.summary: The options in effect.

patch.summary:
Sets and removes runtime overrides. They last across restarts until they expire, are
removed, or the files change the value under them; with `expiresIn` `restart` they are kept
in memory only and end when the daemon stops.

get.summary:
Every option's value with where it came from, one `key=value (source)` line each, secrets
hidden. Needs `debug` and `remote_configuration` on, and someone at the UI.
A configuration file's text, secrets and all.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description:
the file's name, such as `config.d/10-shares.toml`; the first configuration file when
not given

put.summary: Replaces the whole text of a configuration file, then reloads.

patch.summary: Changes some keys of a configuration file, keeping its comments, then reloads.

get.summary: Where a configuration file is.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description:
the file's name, such as `config.d/10-shares.toml`; the first configuration file when
not given

post.summary: Whether a text would load as a configuration file, checked with every other layer.

delete.summary: Removes the runtime override of one key.

get.summary: The options the daemon started with, which every restart-class option still runs with.
Every option with where its value came from, the files, the overrides and what is pending.

Our profile as a user asking for our user info is sent it now: the text, whether a picture
goes with it, and the slots and queue a user we know nothing about is told of, with where
the text and the picture come from.

put.summary: Changes the profile text other users read.

get.summary: The picture other users are sent with our profile.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description:
the picture's tag, so the URL changes whenever the picture does and a cached copy is never
stale; the server does not read it

put.summary:
Sets the picture other users are sent: a JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or BMP image of at most 1 MiB,
kept as a JPEG at most 512 pixels on its longest side.

delete.summary: Stops sending a picture with our profile and removes the one kept.

get.summary: The relay's state: whether it is on, and the agents connected to this controller.
The agents logged in to this controller.

delete.summary:
Closes an agent's connection and unloads its shares; it connects again unless its
configuration was removed too.

get.summary:
An agent fetches a finished download, named in `X-Relay-Filename-Base64` by its path under
the downloads directory, with the token the controller announced it with.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: the token the download was announced with

parameters.name: X-Relay-Credential
parameters.description: the agent's credential for the token

post.summary:
An agent sends the file (`file`, named by its remote filename) a peer downloads through the
controller, for the upload asked for with `token`; answered once that upload has ended,
with how it ended.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: the token the controller asked with

parameters.name: X-Relay-Credential
parameters.description: the agent's credential for the token

post.summary:
An agent sends its share list (`shares`, JSON) and share database (`database`) for the
upload the controller asked for with `token`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: the token the controller asked with

parameters.name: X-Relay-Credential
parameters.description: the agent's credential for the token

get.summary:
The socket an agent keeps open to its controller, opened with a WebSocket upgrade and the
`reseek-relay-v1` sub-protocol.

The server's list of rooms, asked of it now: public rooms, then private ones we are a
member of, then those we own.
The rooms with stored messages, or the one `room` names.

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: only this room, every room with stored messages when left out

delete.summary: Deletes a room's stored messages.

get.summary: A room's whole stored history as a file to save, JSON or text.

A page of a room's stored messages, oldest first, with the gaps in it; for any room, one we
left included.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: only messages before the one with this `localId`, the newest when left out

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: only messages after the one with this `localId`, the page then holding the oldest of them

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many messages to return, at most 500

parameters.name: includeHidden
parameters.description: also return the messages of users blocked for rooms

get.summary: The rooms we are in, with their unread counts.

post.summary:
Joins a room, creating it, as a private room with `private`, when it does not exist.
Answered 304 when we are in it already.

get.summary: A room we are in, with its users and tickers.

delete.summary: Leaves a room.

post.summary: Adds a member to a private room we own or operate, the body the username as a JSON string.

delete.summary: Takes a member out of a private room we own or operate.

get.summary:
A page of what was said in a room we are in, oldest first, with the gaps where we were not
there to hear it; `before` pages back from a message.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: only messages before the one with this `localId`, the newest when left out

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: only messages after the one with this `localId`, the page then holding the oldest of them

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many messages to return, at most 500

parameters.name: includeHidden
parameters.description: also return the messages of users blocked for rooms

post.summary: Says something in a room, the body a JSON string. It shows once the server sends it back.

put.summary: When a room notifies: every message, mentions only, or never.

post.summary:
Makes a member of a private room we own an operator, the body the username as a JSON
string.

delete.summary: Takes a private room's operator back to member.

put.summary: Marks a room read up to a message.

post.summary: Sets our ticker in a room, the body a JSON string; an empty one clears it.

get.summary: The tickers in a room we are in.
The users in a room we are in.

delete.summary: Gives up our membership of a private room.
Gives up our ownership of a private room and leaves it.
delete.description: The room becomes public without an owner, and its members lose access without being told.

204.description: ownership given up and the room left

get.summary: The searches, without their responses, oldest first unless `order` says otherwise.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many searches to return at most, all when left out

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: the order by `startedAt`, oldest first when left out

post.summary:
Starts a search and answers with its record before any response arrives; the responses
follow on the event stream.

get.summary: One search; `includeResponses` adds its responses.

put.summary: Stops a running search. Answered 304 when it had completed already.

delete.summary: Deletes a search, stopping it first when it runs.

get.summary: One search's responses, empty while it runs.
The connection to the Soulseek server.

put.summary:
Connects to the Soulseek server and keeps reconnecting. Answered 205 when the client was
already trying, which makes it try again at once.

205.description: was trying already; trying again now

delete.summary:
Disconnects from the Soulseek server and stops reconnecting. The body, a JSON string, says
why.

get.summary: Who the caller is, with the browser session it came with.

post.summary: Signs in with a local account's username and password and sets the session cookie.

204.description: signed in; the session cookie is set

get.summary:
Whether there is authentication at all for the caller: false on a trusted network and when
authentication is off.

post.summary:
A token that lets a link load one file for ten minutes, for a browser that cannot send the
session with the link.

Ends the caller's browser session and clears its cookie. For a session from an OpenID
Connect provider that has a logout page, that page is returned for the browser to go to.

get.summary: The ways to sign in the login page offers the caller.
The active browser sessions: the caller's own, or everyone's for an administrator.

delete.summary: Revokes every active browser session but the caller's own.
Revokes one browser session, the caller's own or, for an administrator, anyone's.

get.summary: The shares of every host by host name, this one as `local`.

put.summary:
Starts a scan of this host's shares; `force` reads every file again. The scan's progress is
in the application state.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: read every file again, even ones whose size and modification time are unchanged

delete.summary: Stops the running scan.

get.summary: Everything every host shares, as other users browsing us see it.

The folders of this machine a new share can be picked from, directly in a folder or at the top
of the machine. Files never appear, nor anything a scan would leave out; that and a path that
does not exist answer alike.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: the absolute path of the folder; without it the top of the machine, `/` or the drives

get.summary: One share, on any host.
What one share holds, its own directory included.

Every metric, as JSON keyed by family name when `Accept` prefers JSON, else as Prometheus
text.
The metric families a dashboard shows, keyed by name.

The directories other users downloaded most from us, by how many users did. The window is
everything unless given.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, the first release when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, unbounded when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many rows to return, at least 1; 25 when left out

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many rows to skip, 0 when left out

get.summary:
Transfers in one direction that failed, ordered by when they ended. The window is
unbounded unless given.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: the direction to list, `Download` or `Upload` in any case

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, unbounded when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, unbounded when left out

parameters.name: exception
parameters.description: only transfers that failed with exactly this error message

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: `ASC` or `DESC` by end time, in any case; `DESC` when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many rows to return, at least 1; 25 when left out

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many rows to skip, 0 when left out

get.summary:
Failed transfers in one direction counted by why they failed, most frequent first. The
window is unbounded unless given.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: the direction to count, `Download` or `Upload` in any case

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, unbounded when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, unbounded when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many rows to return, at least 1; 25 when left out

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many rows to skip, 0 when left out

get.summary:
Completed transfers by time bucket, direction and outcome, every bucket listed and keyed by
its start, which is a multiple of the bucket's length since the Unix epoch. The window is
the last 7 days unless given, in 100 buckets unless `buckets` or `interval` (minutes) says
otherwise. A bucket's `averageSpeed` is its bytes over its transfers' time.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
the start of the window, seven days ago when left out; a start before the first release
means the oldest transfer

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, exclusive, now when left out

parameters.name: buckets
parameters.description:
how many buckets to divide the window into, from 1 to 1000; 100 when neither this nor
`interval` is given

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: the width of a bucket in minutes, at least 1

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: only this direction, `Download` or `Upload` in any case; both when left out

get.summary:
Users ranked by their successful transfers in one direction. The window is everything
unless given.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: the direction to rank, `Download` or `Upload` in any case

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, the first release when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, now when left out

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: the column to rank by, in any case; `Count` when left out

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: `ASC` or `DESC` in any case, `DESC` when left out

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many rows to return, at least 1; 25 when left out

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many rows to skip, 0 when left out

get.summary: Completed transfers by direction and outcome. The window is the last 7 days unless given.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, seven days ago when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, now when left out

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: only this direction, `Download` or `Upload` in any case; both when left out

get.summary:
One user's transfers by direction: outcomes, totals and why they failed. The window is
everything unless given.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: the start of the window, the first release when left out

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: the end of the window, inclusive, now when left out

get.summary:
The caller's tokens, or everyone's for an administrator, who also sees the configuration's
API keys. Revoked tokens are not listed.

post.summary:
Creates a token with at most the caller's own role. Its secret is in the answer and is
never shown again. Needs a login session: a token cannot make tokens.

put.summary: Renames a token or changes its expiry; the owner's or, for an administrator, anyone's.

delete.summary:
Revokes a token; the owner's or, for an administrator, anyone's. The record is kept a month
for the audit view.

get.summary: Every download, grouped by user and remote directory.

parameters.name: includeRemoved
parameters.description: also list transfers that were removed

delete.summary: Removes every completed download from the listings; the reports still count them.

post.summary: Cancels, removes or retries several downloads in one call.

Enqueues files as one download job, in groups of files from one user each, told of once when
every download of it has ended. The job is refused whole when a group is not valid; a group
refused when it is enqueued, such as one whose user is offline, carries why and leaves the
others enqueued. Answered 201 when every file was enqueued, 207 when some were, and 200 when
none was.

get.summary: A page of downloads, flat, filtered and sorted.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
only transfers in one of these states or categories, any state when empty; repeat the
parameter for several

parameters.name: includeRemoved
parameters.description: also list transfers that were removed

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: only transfers requested at or after this time

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: what the listing is sorted by

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: how many matching transfers to skip

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: how many transfers the page holds at most, up to 1000

get.summary: The downloads from one user, grouped by remote directory.
One download; `includeHistory` adds the states it went through.

color.description: the color the group is shown in, a CSS color name such as `violet`; null for none

priority.description: the group's upload priority, a lower number served first

source.description: why the user is in it

UserInfo.description: What a peer says about itself, as `GET /users/{username}/info` returns it.

description.description: the peer's free text, may be empty

hasFreeUploadSlot.description: the peer has an upload slot free

picture.description: the picture's bytes as the peer sent them, base64; null without one

queueLength.description: how many uploads the peer has queued

uploadPermitted.description:
who may upload to the peer: 0 no one, 1 everyone, 2 users in their list, 3 users they
permitted; null when the peer did not say

UserList.description: One page of the known-users directory.

total.description: how many users match, on every page together

UserNotes.description: Our private notes about a user, the body of `PUT /users/{username}/notes`.

figures.description: what we did with the user

oneOf.description: the last info fetched, null when never

notes.description: our private notes about the user

UserProfile.description: Everything known about a user, the reply of `GET /users/{username}/profile`.

UserRemoved.description: A user was deleted from the directory, the data of a `users.removed` frame.

UserResponse.description:
One peer's transfers in one direction, grouped by remote directory, in the order the
transfers were first asked for.

directories.description: the remote directories the peer's transfers are in, empty when there are none

UserSort.description: What the user directory is sorted by.

privileges.description: our privileges as the server reports them

statistics.description: our statistics as the server reports them

status.description: whether we are online or away, as others see us while we are logged in

UserStatistics.description: A user's statistics as the Soulseek server keeps them.

averageSpeed.description: average upload speed in bytes per second

UserStatus.description: A user's presence and privilege state as the server reports it.

presence.description: whether the user is online, away or offline

UserStatusChanged.description:
A user's presence changed, the data of a `users.status` frame. Sent only for our buddies and
users with an open conversation or a transfer.

activeTransfers.description: transfers with the user that are queued or moving

description.description:
the first three lines of the description in the last info fetched, null when never
fetched

figures.description: what we did with the user

oneOf.description: the last info fetched without the description, null when never

notes.description: the first two lines of our private notes about the user, null when there are none

unreadMessages.description: private messages from the user not acknowledged

UserSummary.description:
A user as the directory lists them, the data of a `users.updated` frame and the reply of
`GET /users/{username}/summary`. Built from stored data only.

UserTags.description: Our labels for a user, the body of `PUT /users/{username}/tags`.

tags.description: at most 32 tags, each 1 to 32 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-` after lower-casing

UserTransferStatistics.description: Outcome counts of one direction of a user report.

errored.description: the ones that errored, timed out, were rejected or aborted

UserTransfers.description: One page of a user's transfers, newest first, removed ones included.

total.description: how many transfers match, on every page together

by.description: the subject of the principal that removed the block, null when it expired

username.description: the user who is no longer blocked

version.description: the shape version of this event type, 0

Validation.description: Whether a text would load as the configuration, checked together with every other layer.

errors.description: why it would not, empty when it would

warnings.description: keys, flags and variables that would be ignored

VersionInfo.description: The running version and whether a newer one exists.

full.description: the version with its build information

isCanary.description: a canary build, which is not checked for updates

isDevelopment.description: a development build, which is not checked for updates

isUpdateAvailable.description: whether `latest` is newer than `current`, null while unknown

latest.description: the latest released version, null until the release feed was read

oneOf.description: a session from a local account's password login
a session from an OpenID Connect login
a session from a trusted reverse proxy's forwarded identity
an API token presented with the request
an API key from the configuration presented with the request

name.description:
the key's name in the configuration, `primary` for the single key given by
environment variable or command line

oneOf.description: the client's address is in a trusted network, so no credential was needed

cidr.description: the configured network the address matched

Via.description: How a request's identity was established.

WaveformTile.description:
The header of a waveform response, which the buckets follow: two signed bytes each, the
lowest and the highest sample over the channels from -127 (full scale below) to 127.

fromSeconds.description: when the first bucket starts, in seconds from the start of the file

peaks.description: how many buckets follow, evenly spread from `fromSeconds` to `toSeconds`

toSeconds.description: when the last bucket ends, in seconds from the start of the file

unread.description: runs of buckets the analysis did not read, as the first and one past the last

WindowSpectra.description:
The header of a window spectra response, which every analyzed window's spectrum over its
second follows, in the order of the report's windows: `bins` bytes each, lowest first, a
byte a level from `minDb` (0) to `maxDb` (255).

bins.description: how many frequency bins a spectrum has, from 0 Hz to `maxHz`

maxDb.description: the level of byte 255, in dB relative to a full-scale sine

maxHz.description: the frequency at the top of the highest bin, in Hz

minDb.description: the level of byte 0, in dB relative to a full-scale sine

WindowSpectrum.description: The spectrum of one analyzed window, as `GET .../analysis/windows/{index}` answers it.

db.description: the level at each point, in dB relative to a full-scale sine, at least -160

hz.description: the frequency of each point, in Hz, lowest first: the middle of each frequency bin

index.description: the window's position in the report's windows

t.description: where the window starts, in seconds from the start of the file
